questions.hint: Add place by place. Do you need to regroup?
questions.solution: Ones: 4 + 1 = 5. Tens: 3 + 2 = 5. Hundreds: 2 + 3 = 5. Thousands: 1 + 4 = 5. The sum is 5,555.

questions.prompt:
What number makes this true?
45 ÷ ___ = 9
questions.hint: 9 times what number is 45?
questions.solution: 9 × 5 = 45, so 45 ÷ 5 = 9. The missing number is 5.

questions.prompt: How many hours are in 2 days?
questions.hint: One day has 24 hours.

questions.prompt: Ivy is older than Jo. Jo is older than Kai. Kai is older than Lu. Who is the second oldest?
questions.hint: Line them up from oldest to youngest.
questions.solution: Oldest to youngest: Ivy, Jo, Kai, Lu. Jo is second oldest.

questions.prompt: What is 1,000 ÷ 8?
questions.hint: Half of 1,000 is 500. Keep halving.
questions.solution: 1,000 ÷ 2 = 500, 500 ÷ 2 = 250, 250 ÷ 2 = 125. Halving 3 times is the same as dividing by 8, so the answer is 125.

questions.prompt: A square and a rectangle have the same perimeter. The rectangle is 10 cm long and 6 cm wide. How long is each side of the square?
questions.hint: Find the perimeter of the rectangle first.
questions.solution: Rectangle perimeter: 10 + 6 + 10 + 6 = 32 cm. The square has 4 equal sides: 32 ÷ 4 = 8 cm.

questions.prompt:
What number comes next in this pattern?
1, 2, 4, 7, 11, 16, ___
questions.hint: Look at how much is added each time: +1, +2, +3, …
questions.solution: The pattern adds 1, then 2, then 3, then 4, then 5. Next it adds 6: 16 + 6 = 22.

questions.prompt: The bar graph shows how many kids chose each Halloween costume. What fraction of the kids chose the ghost costume? Write it in lowest terms.
questions.hint: First find how many kids voted in all.
questions.solution: Total votes: 8 + 12 + 6 + 10 = 36. Ghost got 12 of the 36 votes: 12/36 = 1/3.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest number you can add to 247 to get a multiple of 6?
questions.hint: Find the multiple of 6 just above 247.
questions.solution: 6 × 41 = 246, which is less than 247. The next multiple is 6 × 42 = 252. 252 − 247 = 5.

questions.prompt: How many seconds are in a quarter of an hour?
questions.hint: A quarter of an hour is 15 minutes.
questions.solution: 15 minutes × 60 seconds = 900 seconds.

questions.prompt: A sunflower is 10 cm tall on Day 1. It grows 3 cm every day. On which day will it be 40 cm tall?
questions.hint: How many cm does it need to grow? How many days does that take?
questions.solution: It needs to grow 40 − 10 = 30 cm, which takes 30 ÷ 3 = 10 more days. Day 1 + 10 days = Day 11.

questions.prompt: A café has 3 kinds of soup and 4 kinds of sandwiches. A lunch can be one soup, one sandwich, or one soup with one sandwich. How many different lunches are possible?
questions.hint: Count the three kinds of lunches separately, then add.
questions.solution: Soup only: 3. Sandwich only: 4. Soup and sandwich: 3 × 4 = 12. Total: 3 + 4 + 12 = 19 lunches.

questions.prompt: Leo has $3.45. Mia has $2.80. How much more money does Leo have than Mia?
questions.hint: Subtract: 3.45 − 2.80. Line up the decimal points.

questions.prompt: A round pizza is cut into 8 equal slices from the center. How many degrees is the angle at the point of each slice?
questions.hint: All the slices together make a full turn around the center.
questions.solution: A full turn is 360 degrees. 360 ÷ 8 = 45 degrees.

questions.prompt: Two number cubes, each numbered 1 to 6, are rolled, one red and one blue. In how many different ways can the two numbers add up to 7?
questions.hint: List the red number and the blue number: 1 and 6, 2 and 5, …
questions.solution: Red-blue pairs: 1-6, 2-5, 3-4, 4-3, 5-2, 6-1. That is 6 ways.

questions.prompt: A farmer had a pile of pumpkins. In the morning he sold half of them plus 2 more. In the afternoon he sold half of what was left plus 2 more. He had 4 pumpkins left. How many pumpkins did he start with?
questions.hint: Undo the afternoon first: before selling the extra 2, he had 4 + 2.
questions.solution: Afternoon: 4 + 2 = 6 is half of what he had, so he had 12 at noon. Morning: 12 + 2 = 14 is half of what he started with, so he started with 28. Check: sell 14 + 2 = 16, leaving 12; sell 6 + 2 = 8, leaving 4. ✓

questions.prompt: Ruby writes all the whole numbers from 1 to 50. How many times does she write the digit 3?
questions.hint: Count 3s in the ones place and 3s in the tens place separately.
questions.solution: Ones place: 3, 13, 23, 33, 43, which is 5 times. Tens place: 30 to 39, which is 10 times. Total: 5 + 10 = 15 times (33 has two 3s).

questions.prompt: A rectangle of paper is 12 inches by 8 inches. Kai cuts it into squares that are all the same size, with no paper left over. He uses the largest squares possible. How many squares does he get?
questions.hint: The side of each square must divide both 12 and 8.
questions.solution: The largest number that divides both 12 and 8 is 4, so each square is 4 by 4. Along the 12-inch side: 3 squares. Along the 8-inch side: 2 squares. 3 × 2 = 6 squares.

questions.prompt: Five kids line up for a photo. Ana and Ben want to stand next to each other. How many different ways can the five kids line up?
questions.hint: Glue Ana and Ben together into one block. Then remember the block can be Ana-Ben or Ben-Ana.
questions.solution: Treat Ana and Ben as one block. Now there are 4 things to line up: 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24 ways. Inside the block they can stand Ana-Ben or Ben-Ana, so 24 × 2 = 48 ways.

questions.prompt: Ann and Bob are 40 blocks apart. They walk toward each other at the same time. Ann walks 3 blocks per minute and Bob walks 5 blocks per minute. After how many minutes will they meet?
questions.hint: How much closer do they get each minute?
questions.solution: Each minute they get 3 + 5 = 8 blocks closer. 40 ÷ 8 = 5 minutes.
